newsitem.title: USA: Triarc sees end to Snapple sales slide.
newsitem.headline: Triarc sees end to Snapple sales slide.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Nelson Peltz said on Tuesday sales of its recently acquired Snapple beverages were higher in July and he believed the line had regained its stride.

"Snapple sales in July, which was the first month we really had 100 percent control of Snapple, were up almost three percent," Peltz said in an interview with CNBC. "So far, the sales are trending up again in August."

Triarc bought the Snapple line of ready-to-drink teas and juices from Quaker Oats Co for $300 million in a deal that closed in May. Quaker lost money on the premium beverage unit after buying it about two and a half years ago.
Triarc's other businesses include Arby's restaurants, Mistic and Royal Crown beverage brands.

When asked if he thought the slide in Snapple sales had been arrested, Peltz said: "Yes...We're very pleased, the distributors are very excited and we think we have a hit on our hands." He said premium beverage comparisons were also very difficult during July and August.
To preserve Snapple's space on store shelves, Peltz said Triarc would introduce new products, packages and platforms, or groups of products.
The company planned to introduce 100 percent fruit juices in smaller bottles and had developed three types of green teas in light green bottles, Peltz said.
Triarc would also continue to eye both large and small acquisitions in the fast-food franchising and beverage businesses, he told CNBC.
On Monday, Triarc said in a statement it expected annualized sales of nearly $1 billion from its consumer brands in beverages and its Arby's restaurant chain.
